key_insight: Continual learning for deepfake detection can worsen fairness over time, so preserving accuracy alone is not enough to ensure socially reliable models.
engineering_relevance: For deployed AI security systems, the choice of continual learning strategy affects both detection robustness and demographic equity, making fairness a design constraint rather than an afterthought.
method: Evaluated continual learning on a chronological sequence of 11 real-world deepfake generation methods.
Tracked four fairness dimensions across diverse demographic groups and intersections over time.
Compared CL family approaches including rehearsal, prompts, and regularization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports time-evolving fairness and accuracy measurements across 11 generation methods, showing that accuracy drops often coincide with increased unfairness and that fairness gains are rare.
watch_item: Fairness improvements may not generalize across demographic intersections, so class balance or rehearsal alone may not prevent inequitable forgetting.
paper_title: Time to Fake It: Continual Machine Learning Intensifies Unfairness in Deepfake Detection
